column1: # R1650 — the pointer-reach ratchet's budget. One row per widget whose own
# centre no widget answers: a press there is resolved to a tag nothing
# receives and dropped in silence, so that control is dead to a real mouse
# while every wire-driven assertion about it passes.
# The gate (tools/rpc_verify.py, at every demo's boot) refuses a victim that
# is NOT listed here. A row may be removed by the round that repairs it and
# must never be added to make a failure go away — that is the one use that
# turns a ratchet back into a suggestion.
# Measured 2026-08-11 over 222 example packages: 213 answered, 9 cannot boot
# headless here at all (four terminal arms, an audio-device demo, two
# cross-repo consumers, and two that serve no RPC at boot) and are listed at
# the foot of this file rather than left as a silent remainder. Of the 213,
# EIGHTEEN had a widget nobody can press. Two were repaired in the round that
# measured them (hello-badge, hello-status-bar — a text region that had grown
# over its own widget, repaired by declaring it `pointer_transparent`, which
# is what a label is). The 16 below are the honest remainder.
# ★ The first pass reported 14, and the four it missed were hidden by a defect
# in the GATE ITSELF: raising from `__enter__` leaked the refused subprocess,
# and the leaked binaries starved every launch after them. The round's own
# changelog carries the wrong diagnosis for that (it blamed the terminal arms
# and GPU memory); this file carries the re-measurement, which is what a
# The two repairs this population takes:
#   * pure decoration over a widget -> `pointer_transparent` on the decoration
#   * a real sub-REGION of one widget -> tag it `widget#sub` so the router
#     resolves the widget and the region stays hit-testable (a cursor hint on
#     a resize grip needs that, and transparency would take it away)
# Cannot be measured here, and each says why rather than being dropped:
#   ai-introspect-demo, forge-counter   serve no RPC at boot
#   hello-*-tui (4)                     terminal arms, no pointer surface at all
